entries.title: Right now
entries.detail: Sampled once a second while this page is open. Memory counts what is not available — the page cache is reclaimable and doesn't count.

entries.title: Your palette
entries.detail: Sixteen slots. Everything in the shell is drawn from these — point at one to read its value.

entries.title: Lock while playing
entries.detail: While music plays, a new wallpaper or scheme doesn't overwrite the cover's colours.

entries.title: Tint media cards
entries.detail: Works on its own: the media cards take the cover's colours even when the shell doesn't follow the album.

entries.title: Accent
entries.detail: The fallback colour, for widgets that ask for one. Picked by role, so it follows the next wallpaper.

entries.title: Your bar
entries.detail: Click a module to change it

entries.title: Not on the bar
entries.detail: Drag one straight up onto the bar, or click it to drop it somewhere sensible. Drag a module off the bar onto this card to take it off.

entries.title: Panel placement
entries.detail: Which side of the bar each panel drops from. Each one defaults to the side its own bar module sits on.

entries.title: Resized panels
entries.detail: Drag a panel's outer bottom corner to resize it. Click one here to put it back to its default size.

entries.title: Panel backdrop
entries.detail: Soft cookie shapes drifting behind every panel. They hold still when animations are switched off, and cost nothing while no panel is open.

entries.title: Cookies on the bar, sidebar & frame
Size
entries.detail: Small, Normal and Big move thickness, roundness, inset and the text and icon scales together. Any slider takes you off them, to Custom.

entries.title: Opacity
entries.detail: Translucency needs a compositor blur behind it — Hyprland's is in Desktop › Tuning.

entries.title: Text
entries.detail: How big the bar's text runs — the clock, the workspace numbers, labels.

entries.title: Icons
entries.detail: How big the bar's icons run. Separate from text: a glyph is an icon that happens to be a character.

entries.title: Anchor on workspaces
entries.detail: Keeps the workspace dots at the exact centre of the screen, however wide the modules either side of them grow.

entries.title: Presets
entries.detail: The whole bar, saved under a name: what is on it and every size on this page.

entries.title: Health
entries.detail: How much of the battery's original capacity is left.

entries.title: Power mode
entries.detail: Trades battery life against how hard the machine will work.

entries.title: Battery saver
entries.detail: Rests the cava background, wallpaper effects, floating cookies and the beat clock, and caps Wallpaper Engine at 30 fps. Animations stay.

entries.title: No adapter
entries.detail: No Bluetooth adapter was found, or BlueZ isn't running.

entries.title: Recorder
entries.detail: Clipping keeps a replay buffer running — across reloads and reboots — so Alt+F10 always has something to save.

entries.title: Separate tracks
entries.detail: On, the mic gets a track of its own, for editing. Players, browsers and Discord play only the first track — export with Mixed audio to share.

entries.title: Capture
entries.detail: Focused follows whichever monitor you're on when it starts. Portal asks once through the desktop portal and remembers.

entries.title: Replay buffer
entries.detail: How far back a clip can reach. In quality mode its size follows what's on screen; bitrate mode fixes it.

entries.title: Quality
entries.detail: Constant quality stays sharp in motion and its size varies. A fixed bitrate gives a predictable file and buffer size.

entries.title: Peek
entries.detail: A saved clip opens a card beside the sidebar button for a moment, with its thumbnail.

entries.title: Notify
entries.detail: Also send a notification per saved clip — for when the sidebar is hidden.

entries.title: Files
entries.detail: H.264 in MP4 plays everywhere (Discord and browsers don't play HEVC); Auto picks H.264. MKV survives a crash mid-recording; MP4 doesn't.

entries.title: Name by game
entries.detail: Name a clip after the window you cut it in, so the library can group by game. A game under Steam, Proton

entries.title: Clip & record
entries.detail: Keep recording a few seconds after you press Clip it — so a play you only reacted to afterwards is in the clip.

entries.title: Preview
entries.detail: Drawn by the script that draws the theme, in the colours below. Hyprland's cursor repaints at once; GTK, Qt and XWayland windows pick new colours up the next time they open.

entries.title: Look
entries.detail: The fill colour and the size. The outline is always the shell's background colour.

entries.title: Presets
entries.detail: Colour, size and motion tuning, saved under a name. Loading one never turns the cursor theme or the plugin on or off.

entries.title: Motion effects
entries.detail: Tilt, rotate or stretch the pointer as it moves, with the hypr-dynamic-cursors plugin.

entries.title: Shake to find
entries.detail: Part of the motion plugin: a quick shake makes the pointer big for a moment, so you can find it.

entries.title: Sign-in
entries.detail: How the shell talks to Discord, so the sidebar's Voice module can mute, deafen and screen share.

entries.title: Your own application
entries.detail: About a minute, once

entries.title: Screen share & camera
entries.detail: Discord has no RPC command for these, so the shell presses Discord's own keybind. Set the same combinations as Discord → Settings → Keybinds; screen share has no default.

entries.title: Use the AI title
entries.detail: Instead of the short session name

entries.title: Claude Code
entries.detail: Shows what you're doing in Claude Code as your Discord status. It needs a separate app you register — a client id, nothing else.

entries.title: Counter-Strike 2
entries.detail: Shows your match as your Discord status. No app to set up — it uses Valve's own.

entries.title: Arrangement
entries.detail: Drag a screen to move it; click one to edit it below

entries.title: On
entries.detail: Turn a screen off without unplugging it. At least one has to stay on.

entries.title: Variable refresh rate
entries.detail: Adaptive sync (FreeSync / G-Sync compatible). Only on screens that support it.

entries.title: Your dock
entries.detail: Click an app to open it or go to its next window; Shift-click for a new one; middle-click closes its newest window.

entries.title: Style
entries.detail: ii is End-4's dock: flat rounded buttons, up to three dots under an app (one per window), hairlines between groups, a keep button before the apps (when the sidebar auto-hides — it holds the dock out) and an overview button after them. It has no magnification.

entries.title: Previews
entries.detail: Hover an app for a live thumbnail of each of its windows.

entries.title: Peek
entries.detail: Rest on a window in a preview to glance at its workspace, with that window lit.

entries.title: Melting
entries.detail: Previews and the right-click menu melt out of the dock, inside its length, instead of floating above it.

entries.title: Inner pill
entries.detail: Running apps sit on a pill, neighbours sharing one — like the bar's workspaces.

entries.title: Cap
entries.detail: How much of the edge the dock may take before it scrolls.

entries.title: Pinned
entries.detail: Pin from an app's right-click menu in the dock. Reorder by dragging on the dock itself. Shared with the launcher.

entries.title: Preview
entries.detail: Two tiled windows drawn from your live config: gaps, border, rounding and opacity.

entries.title: Shape
entries.detail: Gaps, borders and how opaque a window is. Written to your Hyprland config when you let go of a slider.

entries.title: Blur & shadow
entries.detail: What sits behind a translucent window — the one thing the preview can't show.

entries.title: Window wobble
entries.detail: Windows stretch like jelly while you drag or resize them. Needs Hyprland 0.57 or newer.

entries.title: Snap floating windows
entries.detail: SUPER-drag a floating window to an edge or corner to fill a half, a quarter or the screen.

entries.title: Snap windows to the widget grid
entries.detail: A floating window you SUPER-drag lands on the same grid as your desktop widgets (set in Desktop › Widgets). Dropping in a zone above still wins.

entries.title: Input
entries.detail: Pointer and focus behaviour, and the keyboard layouts Hyprland starts with.

entries.title: Animations
entries.detail: Each animation's speed (lower is faster), and whether it runs at all.

entries.title: Your layouts
entries.detail: The bar's keyboard pill cycles these, in this order. To reorder, remove one and add it back — it goes to the end. Applied with hyprctl, so a Hyprland restart brings back what your config says.

entries.title: Key repeat
entries.detail: What a held-down key does: how soon it starts repeating, and how fast.

entries.title: Speed
entries.detail: Hyprland's sensitivity: 0 is the device's own speed.

entries.title: Acceleration
entries.detail: Adaptive speeds up with faster movement; Flat keeps it 1:1 (what most players want).

entries.title: Left-handed
entries.detail: Swaps the primary and secondary buttons.

entries.title: Mouse
entries.detail: Applies to every pointer. Saved to hardware.lua; Reload in the bar above applies it.

entries.title: Natural scrolling
entries.detail: Content follows your fingers, like a phone.

entries.title: Tap and drag
entries.detail: Tap, then keep the finger down to drag.

entries.title: Ignore while typing
entries.detail: The touchpad pauses briefly after a key press, so a palm doesn't move the cursor.

entries.title: Two-finger right-click
entries.detail: Click with two fingers for a right-click and three for a middle-click, instead of by where you press.

entries.title: Touchpad
entries.detail: Laptop touchpads. Saved to hardware.lua; Reload in the bar above applies it.

entries.title: Shell language
entries.detail: The language of the shell's own text. Only strings that have been prepared for translation change; everything else stays in English. To add a language, copy translations/en_US.json to a new <code>.json and translate the right-hand sides.

entries.title: Current
entries.detail: What the system reports right now. Picking a locale below sets the language, date and number formats programs start with — it needs your password, and running programs keep the old one until they restart.

entries.title: Prefixes
entries.detail: Typed into the launcher's empty field, a prefix switches its mode: > runs a command, ? asks, + installs a package, ; searches your clipboard, : finds an emoji. Sums, unit conversions and site shortcuts (yt cats) just work.

entries.title: Rows shown
entries.detail: How many results fit before the list scrolls. The card grows by a row each.

entries.title: Results
entries.detail: What it answers, and how much of it

entries.title: Model
entries.detail: Empty is the provider's default. Change it if a provider starts answering 404.

entries.title: Session
entries.detail: Kept between questions

entries.title: Search the web first
entries.detail: Gemini only. The question also reaches the search backend.

entries.title: Ask
entries.detail: Start a launcher line with ? to ask. Nothing is sent until you press Enter. Off, ? opens a web search in your browser instead.

entries.title: Search engine
entries.detail: The address a web search opens; %s is replaced by what you typed.

entries.title: Engine name
entries.detail: What the launcher calls it where it offers a search.

entries.title: History
entries.detail: Apps you open often rise within equally good matches. Only app ids and counts are kept — never what you typed.

entries.title: Run & search
entries.detail: > runs a command in a terminal. A search that finds no app offers the web search instead.

entries.title: Site shortcuts
entries.detail: Type a key, a space, then what to search

entries.title: What it shows
entries.detail: Everything on the lock screen is readable by whoever is standing at the machine.

entries.title: Animate the scene
entries.detail: Off holds one frame of the scene's preview — the only real cure for its short loop.

entries.title: Background
entries.detail: What sits behind the clock. A running Wallpaper Engine scene shows as its blurred preview — the renderer publishes no still of the live frame.

entries.title: Lock before sleep
entries.detail: Locks as the machine suspends or hibernates, so it wakes to the lock screen.

entries.title: Lock when idle
entries.detail: Leave this off until you've tested unlocking. The bar's idle pill and gamemode hold it off.

entries.title: Profile picture
entries.detail: Lock screen only — nothing is written to ~/.face.

entries.title: Authentication
entries.detail: Which PAM stack the password box asks. \"login\" exists everywhere. If the lock ever refuses a correct password: Ctrl+Alt+F2, log in, and run loginctl unlock-session.

entries.title: Motion
entries.detail: How far each word travels as it is sung — never the timing, which stays keyed to the vocal. Point at the line to play it.

entries.title: Look up as a fallback
entries.detail: Asks NetEase and LRCLIB when the Spotify bridge has nothing. It sends the artist, title and album.

entries.title: Source
entries.detail: Which provider answered for the current track, and whether the shell may look lyrics up itself.

entries.title: Translation
entries.detail: Which service translates, and its optional API key.

entries.title: Radio blocked
entries.detail: A kill switch or function key holds Wi-Fi off

entries.title: Wi-Fi
entries.detail: Join, forget, or connect to a hidden network.

entries.title: Speed test
entries.detail: What the link can carry, measured only when you press Run. It contacts a third party and moves real data, so both are named under the trace.

entries.title: DNS
entries.detail: Which resolver answers your lookups. Changing it reconnects the link for a moment.

entries.title: Needs a backend
entries.detail: Install one, then reload the shell

entries.title: Temperature
entries.detail: Lower is warmer. 6500K is daylight — no change at all.

entries.title: Fixed times
entries.detail: From and until, as HH:MM. Crossing midnight (20:00 until 07:00) is the normal case.

entries.title: This week
entries.detail: App names and minutes, kept on this computer only — never window titles.

entries.title: Away after
entries.detail: With no input for this long, you count as away and the clock stops.

entries.title: What counts
entries.detail: The focused window's app counts while you're at the machine. Idle time doesn't, unless something keeps the screen awake (a video playing). Locked time never does.

entries.title: Keep
entries.detail: Days older than this are dropped.

entries.title: Set up
entries.detail: Packages, the morphing plugin, Hyprland wiring, app theming and the optional extras — tick what you want and press the one button. The same thing the first-run window shows.

entries.title: Checks
entries.detail: How Hyprland is wired, the optional tools, Spotify's bridge and where secrets live. Tap one that needs attention for its fix.

entries.title: Shell presets
entries.detail: Every settings page, saved under a name; tap one to apply it. To use it on another machine: commit presets/shell.json, git pull there, and tap it. Bar presets (presets/bar.json) and desktop-widget placement (widgets.json) are their own files — commit them too if you want them.

entries.title: Preview
entries.detail: A card drawn at your settings, from the shell's real components. Everything on this page changes it.

entries.title: Text
entries.detail: The font for labels, titles and body copy everywhere in the shell.

entries.title: Numerals
entries.detail: The font for throughput, timers and other figures that must line up. A monospace face is best.

entries.title: Display
entries.detail: The font for the big clock on the lock and login screens. Heavier faces read best.

entries.title: Spacing
entries.detail: How tightly everything packs: padding, gaps, row heights.

entries.title: Roundness
entries.detail: Corner radius of cards, panels and controls. The bar and desktop widgets keep their own.

entries.title: Opacity
entries.detail: How much of the desktop shows through the shell's surfaces.

entries.title: Shadows
entries.detail: How far surfaces float. At zero the shell stops drawing shadows altogether.

entries.title: Motion
entries.detail: Every animation in the shell — panels, notifications, the lock screen, the bar — runs through these two.

entries.title: Settings window
entries.detail: Window: a floating window the compositor places, like any other app. Panel: pinned to the bottom edge and merged into the frame, so it never covers the bar.

entries.title: On the sidebar
entries.detail: Tap one to put it on the sidebar or take it off. The dock, stats and clips have tabs of their own, with their switch in the heading.

entries.title: Edge & size
entries.detail: The bar owns the top edge; the sidebar takes one of the other three. Everything on it is sized around the dock's icons.

entries.title: Auto-hide
entries.detail: Rest the pointer on the edge, or press Super+D (by default), to bring it back.

entries.title: Dodge windows
entries.detail: A kind of auto-hide: the sidebar stays out until a window would sit under it.

entries.title: Empty workspaces
entries.detail: Nothing to cover and nothing else to look at, so the sidebar and its dock stay out until a window opens. (End-4's rule.)

entries.title: Edge reveal
entries.detail: Turn this off to stop the sidebar popping out whenever the pointer brushes the edge — combine it with Empty workspaces and the dock's keep button.

entries.title: Reserve space
entries.detail: Tiled windows leave the sidebar's edge free. Off while auto-hide is on — it would reserve an empty strip.

entries.title: Look
entries.detail: Islands give each group its own pill. The hero sits on a tinted chip, as the top bar's clock does. The music makes the pills breathe and glow while something plays.

entries.title: Clipboard
entries.detail: Copies a password manager marks as secret never reach the history, so they never peek.

entries.title: Peeks
entries.detail: When something happens to a module, a card opens beside it for a moment — on the monitor you're on, and never over a panel you opened.

entries.title: Arrange
entries.detail: Drag one onto the sidebar, along it to move it, onto another to group them, or off it onto this card to take it off.

entries.title: Readings
entries.detail: The button shows the first three

entries.title: Temperatures
entries.detail: An inner arc on the CPU and GPU rings showing the temperature, 0–100°C.

entries.title: Split network
entries.detail: Download on the network ring's outer arc, upload on the inner one.

entries.title: Line speed
entries.detail: What a full network ring means. Fixed, so an idle link never looks busy.

entries.title: Alerts
entries.detail: A ring held over its threshold says so in its card. CPU and memory alert on load, the temperatures on degrees.

entries.title: System monitor
entries.detail: What a middle-click on the stats button, or on a reading in its panel, opens. Right-clicking the button opens this page.

entries.title: Mixer
entries.detail: Off until you turn it on. Every sound is generated on this machine (scripts/gen-sfx.py) — nothing is downloaded.

entries.title: Output
entries.detail: Where sound goes, and how loud. Click the speaker to mute; scroll over the level to step it.

entries.title: Input
entries.detail: What the machine can hear. Test plays your microphone back through the output, so you hear how you actually sound — headphones only, or it howls.

entries.title: Applications
entries.detail: Per-app volume, and which device each one plays on. It is a PipeWire stream property — it follows the app, not this page.

entries.title: Peak caps
entries.detail: A cap over each bar that holds, then falls

entries.title: Glow
entries.detail: A soft light round it, in its colour

entries.title: Album cover
entries.detail: The cover inside the ring while music plays

entries.title: Desktop visualiser
entries.detail: A live spectrum of what's playing, pinned behind your windows.

entries.title: Recording
entries.detail: Applications holding the microphone open.

entries.title: Disks
entries.detail: Each disk's used space against its size. The root disk is broken down by what fills it; Other is everything not measured on its own, and Reserved is the share the filesystem keeps for root — why the numbers seem not to add up.

entries.title: Home folder
entries.detail: Each tile is a folder in your home, as large as its share of the space. Hover one for its path. Nothing here is ever deleted for you.

entries.title: Reclaim space
entries.detail: Caches, old package versions and logs — files that rebuild themselves. Orphans are packages nothing needs any more; removing those uninstalls them, so it asks twice.

entries.title: Check for new versions
entries.detail: Every 6 hours

entries.title: Quicktest
entries.detail: Updates to the shell itself — signed releases from GitHub.

entries.title: Discord
entries.detail: Re-patch Vencord

entries.title: Drawn by
entries.detail: Static images only.

entries.title: Depth
entries.detail: How far the clock stays behind when the picture moves, so it slides behind the subject. Needs parallax on.

entries.title: Edge softness
entries.detail: Blurs the edge where the subject covers the clock, so the pixels of the cut-out don't show.

entries.title: Apply images to
entries.detail: Scenes always cover every screen.

entries.title: Music effects
entries.detail: Pictures, and Wallpaper Engine scenes the shell plays from a window (scene preload on). Rests while nothing plays, behind a fullscreen window and in Game Mode.

entries.title: Intensity
entries.detail: How strong everything is at its biggest. The song does the rest: calm parts settle to a soft glow, big parts move, the drop hits hardest, and a busy part (sixteenth hi-hats) plays smaller.

entries.title: Sync
entries.detail: The effects already wait for your speakers. If they still land before the beat you hear (Bluetooth adds more delay than it reports), hold them back further.

entries.title: Sound map
entries.detail: Every sound is on, and the song decides how much each one shows: little in a calm part, all of it in a big one, more on the drop. Slide one to want more or less of it; Auto puts every sound back. Strobe is never on unless you turn it on.

entries.title: Renderer
entries.detail: Options apply on Refresh.

entries.title: Monitors
entries.detail: One scene per screen, or one spanned across several.

entries.title: Library
entries.detail: Blank = the default folder.

entries.title: Add a widget
entries.detail: Click one to place it

entries.title: Bring forward what matters
entries.detail: A running timer, or the music while something plays

entries.title: Grow from centre
entries.detail: Bars extend both ways from the middle, like the bar pill

entries.title: Track card
entries.detail: What's playing, shown when a song starts and when you hover; plus how far through it is

entries.title: Soft edges
entries.detail: Lines fade out at the top and bottom instead of being cut

entries.title: Tile frame
entries.detail: The widget's own fill and outline, around the card

entries.title: Parallax
entries.detail: How far a widget leans and its contents shift under the pointer. Off in the chips above.

entries.title: Snap grid
entries.detail: Widgets you drag snap to this grid.

entries.title: Look
entries.detail: Every widget

entries.title: Weather
entries.detail: Only the place you pick is ever requested — your location is never looked up from your IP. Night light and the calendar use it too.

entries.title: Calendars
entries.detail: Paste a calendar's .ics address — Google: your calendar's settings › Secret address in iCal format — and its events show in the clock panel, read-only, in a colour of their own. The address stays on this machine.

entries.title: Presets
entries.detail: Click a preset to load it once, on the chosen screen. Right-click one to give the screen's wallpaper that preset LIVE instead: switch to the wallpaper and its tiles take over automatically; switch away and your normal ones return. Follows the colour scheme panel's own click-to-load / right-click-to-bind split.
